name: Iddo
overview: Iddo was a male descendant of the tribe of Levi who held a position of leadership at the place called Casiphia. His role as the leading man there highlights his importance within the Levitical community during the time recorded in Ezra 8:17. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Iddo likely means 'YHWH has adorned,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's involvement or blessing. This meaning underscores the spiritual heritage associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Iddo as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the priestly tribe. Additionally, it is inferred from Nehemiah 12:16 that he was the grandfather of Zechariah, linking him to a notable prophetic lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Iddo's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his leadership role among the Levites at Casiphia, indicating his responsibility in the post-exilic community's religious and social organization. His Levitical heritage and connection to Zechariah suggest a continuity of faithful service to God across generations. Though details are sparse, his mention in Ezra highlights his trusted status during the return from exile.
